title: Speculative Speculative Decoding
quote: Unlike ordinary speculative decoding, in SSD the draft model is located on distinct hardware from the target.
proves: Saguaro drafts the next round for predicted verification outcomes while verification runs; draft on 1xH100, target on 4xH100; on a cache miss the entire batch stalls on the latency of the backup speculator; authors state failures happen increasingly often at large batch sizes and temperatures; abstract v3 claims 30% avg over optimized SD, up to 5x over AR; most end-to-end speedup comes from hiding draft latency rather than increasing lookahead.
does_not_prove: Uses an extra GPU (TP=5 vs 4) so cost per token is not compared at equal hardware; batch-size scaling only in a figure vs synchronous baselines; no multi-tenant or shared-GPU evaluation; no accounting of wasted draft compute on mis-predicted outcomes under load.
bearing: Directly threatens 'draft next round during verify' ideas; leaves open who pays for the extra drafter GPU and behaviour under high batch / shared drafter.

title: PEARL: Parallel Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Draft Length
quote: the target model gets stuck when the draft model is guessing tokens, and vice versa
proves: Pre-verify (verify first draft token during drafting) and post-verify (draft more tokens during verification) remove mutual waiting; up to 4.43x over AR and up to 1.50x over vanilla SD.
does_not_prove: Abstract-level; assumes draft and target run in parallel on separate resources; no serving-level batch or load study.
bearing: Prior art for overlapped draft/verify; shrinks novelty of any 'draft during verify' candidate.

title: AMUSD: Asynchronous Multi-Device Speculative Decoding for LLM Acceleration
quote: AMUSD enables both models to perform predictions independently on separate devices (e.g., GPUs).
proves: Continuous asynchronous draft/verify on separate GPUs; avg 29% over SD, up to 1.96x over AR with identical output.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not discuss rollback cost or batching; single-request latency focus.
bearing: Prior art for disaggregated async drafting; supports idea that rollback cost under batching is unstudied.

title: PipeSpec: Breaking Stage Dependencies in Hierarchical LLM Decoding
quote: enabling asynchronous execution with lightweight coordination for prediction verification and rollback
proves: Generalizes SD to k models in a pipeline across devices; claims guaranteed throughput improvement for any non-zero acceptance rate; up to 2.54x on LLaMA 2/3.
does_not_prove: Throughput guarantee is analytical and per-request, on dedicated devices; no shared-GPU or multi-request contention.
bearing: Prior art for multi-level pipelined speculation; threatens cascade-pipeline candidates.

title: SwiftSpec: Ultra-Low Latency LLM Decoding by Scaling Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
quote: redesigns the speculative decoding pipeline in an asynchronous and disaggregated manner
proves: Async disaggregated draft/verify removes draft from critical path; 1.75x avg over SOTA SD systems; Llama3-70B at 348 tok/s on 8 Hopper GPUs; targets single-query / small-batch TP.
does_not_prove: Small-batch latency only; no throughput-per-GPU or multi-tenant evaluation.
bearing: Threatens disaggregated async drafter ideas at batch 1; leaves high-batch and shared-drafter economics open.

title: SpecBranch: Speculative Decoding via Hybrid Drafting and Rollback-Aware Branch Parallelism
quote: the key challenge lies in the trade-offs between parallelization and token rollback
proves: Branch-prediction-inspired parallel speculative branches hedge likely rejections; confidence plus target-feature reuse sets draft length; rollback tokens cut 50% for poorly aligned models; 1.8x-4.5x over AR.
does_not_prove: Hedging branches cost extra compute; no evaluation under serving load where that compute competes with other requests.
bearing: Covers branch-prediction / confidence-estimator analogy; leaves open the cost of hedging at high batch.

title: NebulaSD: Many-for-Many Speculative Decoding
quote: dynamic pooling improves request-round processing rate by 50.4% over a physically disaggregated baseline
proves: M-for-N pooling of draft and target workers with batches rebuilt per stage from shared request pools and async KV-state preparation; +50.4% vs disaggregated, +72.6% vs co-located on 4 GPUs.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; scaling result is from idealized simulation of state movement; does not address mis-speculation waste or tenant isolation.
bearing: Strong threat to 'shared drafter pool / disaggregated drafting' candidates (very recent, Sep 2026).

title: ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batched Self-Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: all requests in a batch share a single draft-verify schedule
proves: Non-synchronized batched self-speculation: batch-aware cost model lets each request choose when to verify; 1.70-4.58x decode throughput over AR; ~27% over best self-spec baselines.
does_not_prove: Self-speculative and long-context only; not a separate-drafter or engine (vLLM/SGLang) integration.
bearing: Threatens 'break lockstep draft/verify in a batch' candidates.

title: DuoDecoding: Hardware-aware Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding with Dynamic Multi-Sequence Drafting
quote: strategically deploys the draft and target models on the CPU and GPU respectively
proves: Draft on CPU, target on GPU, in parallel with a hardware-aware draft budget to minimize idle time; TTFT 83% of conventional SD; up to 2.61x latency speedup.
does_not_prove: Single request; discrete CPU/GPU; nothing on unified memory (Apple silicon) where CPU and GPU share bandwidth.
bearing: Relevant to using idle CPU cores on M5 for drafting; unified-memory contention is open.

title: Cascade Speculative Drafting for Even Faster LLM Inference
quote: The Vertical Cascade eliminates autoregressive generation from neural models,
proves: Multi-level drafting: vertical cascade drafts the drafter; horizontal cascade allocates draft time by position.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; sequential latency focus, no serving load.
bearing: Prior art for cascade/multi-level speculation.

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
quote: benefits from shared compute and activations of the draft and verification stages
proves: Early-exit drafting with remaining layers as verifier; less memory than separate drafter; up to 2.16x on CNN/DM.
does_not_prove: Requires training recipe; no batch/serving study.
bearing: Prior art for early-exit (confidence) drafting.

title: SpecReason: Fast and Accurate Inference-Time Compute via Speculative Reasoning
quote: SpecReason achieves 1.4-3.0
proves: Small model drafts whole reasoning steps; base model assesses/corrects them; 1.4-3.0x speedup with +0.4-9.0% accuracy; combined with SD an additional 8.8-58.0% latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Lossy (semantic not token equivalence); single-request; no serving cost of rejected steps under load.
bearing: Speculation beyond tokens; mis-speculation cost of rejected reasoning steps in shared serving is open.

title: HeteroReason: Heterogeneous FPGA-GPU Acceleration for Disaggregated Speculative Reasoning
quote: the draft model is offloaded to the FPGA while deploying the PRM and target models on GPUs.
proves: Disaggregated speculative reasoning with step-ahead speculation; 1.01x-1.42x latency, 1.25x-1.57x energy efficiency vs homogeneous GPU.
does_not_prove: FPGA-specific; small latency gains; no multi-tenant evaluation.
bearing: Supports 'drafter on separate cheap hardware' line; shows gains can be marginal.

title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
quote: Across domains, we achieve up to 55% next-action prediction accuracy, translating into up to 20% latency reductions.
proves: Fast models predict next agent actions and execute in parallel, committed only when authoritative model agrees; gives a cost-latency analysis of speculative breadth.
does_not_prove: Cost figures not in abstract; does not study the serving engine side (extra requests' effect on other tenants' batches).
bearing: Threatens 'speculative tool calls' candidates; serving-side cost of agent speculation is open.

title: AOSpec: Action and Observation Co-Speculation for Low-Latency Agent Serving
quote: its gains increase as decoding accelerates
proves: Co-speculates actions and observations; side-effecting actions run in isolated forks; 11.8-32.5% mean and up to 42.8% p99 end-to-end latency reduction on Terminal-Bench.
does_not_prove: No detailed serving-cost figures in abstract; isolation is per-environment fork, not GPU/KV.
bearing: Strong threat to agent-level speculation candidates (Aug 2026).

title: Speculate with Memory: Lossless Acceleration for LLM Agents
quote: All speculation is lossless because it runs during idle time at zero added wall-clock cost.
proves: Memory of past trajectories improves action prediction 19-39% relative and observation prediction up to 2.5x.
does_not_prove: 'Zero added wall-clock cost' assumes idle resources; ignores GPU/token cost of speculative calls on a shared server.
bearing: The idle-time assumption is a gap: who pays for agent speculation on loaded servers.

title: Parallelizing Tool Execution and LLM Generation for Low-Latency Agent Serving (PASTE)
quote: PASTE isolates speculative results until confirmed by the LLM
proves: Speculative tool execution during generation; -43.5% avg task completion time; 1.8x lower observed tool latency.
does_not_prove: Abstract silent on mis-speculation cost / wasted tool calls.
bearing: Threatens speculative-tool-call candidates.

title: NVIDIA Dynamo docs: Agents user guide (speculative prefill)
quote: Per-turn TTFT on turns 2+ can drop significantly (e.g. up to ~3× in
proves: After a turn ends, Dynamo can send a speculative max_tokens=1 prefill of the predicted next-turn prefix to the same worker to warm KV; cache prefetching to other workers is listed as future work.
does_not_prove: No statement on wrong predictions, wasted prefill compute, or KV eviction pressure caused by speculative prefill under load.
bearing: Speculative prefill is shipped; its mis-speculation cost and KV-pressure interaction are open.

title: Async Scheduling Plan (vLLM issue #27679)
quote: Follow-on async scheduling + spec decode hardening/compatibility issues
proves: Tracking issue (Oct-Dec 2025) for async scheduling; lists #24799 spec compatibility, #29223 logprobs, #29821 structured outputs; closed via enabling async scheduling by default (#27614).
does_not_prove: Plan only; no performance data.
bearing: Shows async+spec is engine-level active work; context for engine candidates.

title: [Core] Async Scheduling X Spec Decoding Compatibility (vLLM PR #24799)
quote: we won't copy draft token ids to scheduler any more, but cache it in gpu_model_runner
proves: Drafts kept on GPU worker for next step; A100 EAGLE Llama3-8B k=2: +1.8% (24 prompts), +6.2% (48), +7.1% (96) throughput vs sync; only EAGLE supported at merge; blocking sync after drafting accepted as known compromise.
does_not_prove: Small gains; ngram/medusa excluded at merge; no mis-speculation accounting.
bearing: Baseline for vLLM async+spec; gains from overlap are modest.

title: [Async][Spec Decoding] Zero-bubble async scheduling + spec decoding (vLLM PR #32951)
quote: optimistically assuming all draft tokens are accepted on the CPU and deferring the correction until after the forward pass
proves: CPU schedules next step assuming all drafts accepted, GPU tensors are source of truth; DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP k=1 at concurrency 1: TPOT 9.19->8.90 ms, TTFT 62.86->53.30 ms.
does_not_prove: Benchmarked only at concurrency 1 with k=1 (94% acceptance); no data on how optimistic over-allocation behaves at low acceptance or high batch.
bearing: Optimistic placeholder scheduling = systems speculation inside engine; cost of over-reservation under load is open.

title: vLLM v0.19.0 release notes
quote: Async scheduling now supports speculative decoding with zero-bubble overlap, significantly improving throughput
proves: Zero-bubble async+spec shipped in v0.19.0 (#32951).
does_not_prove: Release note claim, no numbers.
bearing: Confirms feature is mainline; any candidate must start from it.

title: [Performance]: Eagle3 speculative decoding latency regression in v0.19 vs v0.18 (vLLM issue #39940)
quote: the regression cuts the spec decode benefit nearly in half
proves: H200 TP=4 Llama-3.1-8B + EAGLE3 k=3 at 1 QPS: TPOT 2.62 ms (v0.18) vs 2.84 ms (v0.19), spec speedup 16.0% -> 8.4%, acceptance unchanged; maintainer traced part to torch.compile of update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change (fix 2.82->2.63 ms) but said not sufficient; closed as stale.
does_not_prove: Single low-load workload; root cause not fully closed.
bearing: Evidence that async+spec bookkeeping (small kernels) eats spec gains; supports measurement-driven candidates.

title: [Bug]: PP + async scheduling + spec decode: output_token_ids trim only runs on the last PP rank (vLLM issue #54260)
quote: With pipeline parallelism, async scheduling and speculative decoding active at the same time, the non-last ranks accumulate an unbounded overshoot
proves: Optimistic extend (assumes all k drafts accepted) never trimmed on non-last PP ranks; NCCL deadlock after ~15 rounds; reproduced on v0.27.1 with PP=2 + MTP k=7; open as of Aug 2026.
does_not_prove: Correctness bug, not a performance study.
bearing: Shows rollback of optimistic state is fragile across ranks; supports 'rollback correctness/cost' angle.

title: [Bug]: json_object structured output not enforced after Qwen thinking with async scheduling + spec decode (vLLM issue #43388)
quote: in async scheduling + speculative decoding, new_token_ids can contain multiple tokens in one step
proves: Multi-token accepted steps plus placeholder offsets made the reasoning-end detector miss </think>, so the grammar was never applied.
does_not_prove: Correctness bug; closed.
bearing: Interaction bugs between optimistic placeholders and per-token state machines.

title: SGLang docs: Speculative Decoding (V2 / overlap scheduler)
quote: The overlap scheduler currently only supports `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`
proves: Spec V2 workers run with overlap scheduler by default; NGRAM and DFLASH disable the overlap scheduler and mixed chunked prefill; topk>1 errors or is incompatible.
does_not_prove: Docs; no performance numbers.
bearing: Shows overlap is limited to chain drafts; tree/ngram overlap is a remaining engine gap.

title: From research to production: Accelerate OSS LLM with EAGLE-3 on Vertex
quote: the overlap scheduler gives us an additional 10% - 20% speedup across the board
proves: CPU launches next Draft and Draft Extend kernels while GPU runs Verify, via a FutureMap; +10-20% on Llama 4 Scout.
does_not_prove: Configuration for the number not given; vendor blog.
bearing: Overlap of CPU scheduling with verify is largely captured already.

title: [Spec] DFlash: remove per-step host syncs so the CPU runs a full step ahead (SGLang PR #31468)
quote: worth **+12–13% tok/s/user at low concurrency and +3–5% at high**
proves: Removing per-step host syncs raised run-ahead fraction 0.88 -> 0.995; gain +12-13% at low concurrency, +3-5% at high; GSM8K and accept length unchanged.
does_not_prove: Single proposer (DFlash); H-class GPU only.
bearing: Quantifies that overlap gains shrink at high concurrency.

title: [SPEC V2] fix: skip stale state updates in spec-v2 overlap (SGLang PR #23456)
quote: only rolls back the pre-claimed bonus slot for finished requests
proves: Under overlap, decode results can arrive after a request finished or was retracted; applying accept_lens to stale requests corrupted KV bookkeeping and spec metrics.
does_not_prove: Bug fix, no measurement.
bearing: Speculative pre-claim of KV slots before acceptance is real engine practice; rollback paths are bug-prone.

title: Fix cross-stream ordering races in spec-v2 overlap plan stream (SGLang PR #28034)
quote: silently degrading accuracy and accept length
proves: With the overlap plan stream on, prepare_for_v2_verify overwrote shared req_to_token cells while draft still read them; under load crashed with illegal memory access; open PR.
does_not_prove: Opt-in flag only; no perf numbers.
bearing: Further evidence that deeper overlap of draft/verify planning hits shared-state hazards.

title: Support spec v2 tree drafting (eagle topk>1) with page_size==1 (SGLang PR #26866)
quote: topk>1 with page_size>1 still falls back to v1.
proves: Tree drafting under overlap scheduler now works only for page_size==1; accepted-KV move had been stubbed.
does_not_prove: No throughput numbers.
bearing: Tree speculation + overlap + paged KV remains incomplete in SGLang.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: while retaining the draft model reduces KV cache capacity, limiting batch size and degrading throughput
proves: SD degrades performance in high-load compute-bound settings; Nightjar disables SD under load and offloads drafter; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% lower latency vs standard SD.
does_not_prove: Adaptive on/off is R04 territory; does not study overlapped/async speculation costs.
bearing: Evidence that speculation hurts at high batch; threatens naive always-on overlap ideas.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: explains why speedups often diminish as server load increases
proves: Latency model infers effective batch size from request rate via Little's Law to explain shrinking SD gains under load.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no thresholds; does not model async/overlapped drafting.
bearing: Supports a model-based answer to 'when does speculation hurt'; async variants not modelled.

title: Batch speculative decoding (EQSPEC) ragged-tensor overhead
proves: Search snippet only: fixing ragged acceptance across a batch adds overhead up to 40% of compute.
does_not_prove: Not opened; venue and numbers unverified.
bearing: Possible cost of per-request acceptance divergence at batch.

title: vLLM v0.18.0 release notes (NGram GPU + async scheduler, #29184)
proves: Search snippet only: NGram speculative decoding runs on GPU and is compatible with the async scheduler.
does_not_prove: Not opened.
bearing: If true, ngram async gap in vLLM is closed (unlike SGLang C26).
